originality.rationale: Directly compared the proved two-ball full regular-simplex statement to both materially inspected primary full-text sources. The 2006 theorem computes coverings of crosspolytopes, which are different convex bodies, and explicitly shows a vertex/full-body covering distinction in dimension three. The 2010 theorem is a finite-set Euclidean three-dimensional 2-center algorithm, with no all-dimensional continuum simplex formula or optimizer parity. Multiple actual mathematical-record and web searches for exact formula, equivalent geometric formulations, aliases and dominance did not identify an implication-equivalent source. Published coordinate-isometry and planar-regular-polygon records do not determine full-simplex two-ball covering. Remaining risk is explicit and independent literature validation remains unperformed.

value.rationale: Motivated by finite Euclidean 2-center optimization and the known failure for the 3D crosspolytope of lifting vertex-only covering to a full polytope. This theorem proves the lift exactly for an entire natural higher-dimensional convex-body family, determines a sharp scale-invariant radius in all dimensions, and gives a complete odd-dimensional optimizer classification with exact counts and positive-dimensional even-dimensional optimality. This structural parity contrast is not implied merely by computing finite face circumradii or by a general algorithm.
